name: Electrical goods (fans, cables, switches, lighting)
shape_facts: Main products: fans, cables/wires, switches/accessories, lighting — or assembled/imported range.
Manufacturer, assembler of imported kits, or brand owner using contract manufacturers.
Sales channel: dealers/electric shops, distributors, projects/contractors, online marketplaces.
Warranty and after-sales handled in-house or through dealers.
Imported components (motors, LED chips, copper, PVC compound) share.
Factory location and size, and number of sales reps.
scope_rule: pi notes business problems: stock, warranty claims, dealer credit, schemes, copper/raw material costs, production, distribution, after-sales and reporting. It gives no electrical safety, wiring, load-rating or product-certification advice and no view on whether products meet standards. It records roles of dealers, electricians and customers, not personal details. Shocks, fires or burns reported mean pi stops and points to emergency services.

vocabulary.winding: copper coil in the fan motor

problems.phrase: Before summer everyone wants fans at once and we can’t produce enough
After summer, thousands of fans sit in the warehouse
Copper prices jump and my cable price list is wrong overnight
Warranty claims come back but we can’t tell if it’s real or customer damage
Dealers send fans back for ‘repair’ that are actually fakes with our name
Cable coils are short in length and dealers complain
Each dealer has a different discount and nobody remembers what was promised
Dealers don’t pay until the next season
Sales reps take orders on WhatsApp and some never reach the factory
LED bulbs fail early and returns are eating margin
Import container of motors or LED chips delayed, line stopped
Daraz listings get bad reviews about delivery damage
Online orders and dealer stock come from the same warehouse and clash
No idea which model is profitable after warranty costs
Electrician loyalty scheme coupons are abused
Copper scrap in the winding section goes missing
Service centre tickets are in a register, nobody follows up
Power outages at the factory stop the assembly line
Brand is unknown outside our city
Serial numbers aren’t recorded, so warranty dates can’t be checked
Assembly line workers are seasonal and need training every year
Freight to distributors in other provinces is expensive
Project tenders need product documents that we keep in random folders
I don’t know daily sales by region until month-end

seasonality: When does your busy season start?
How early do you start building stock?
What happened to leftover stock last year?
warranty: How many claims come in during the season?
How do you check whether a claim is genuine?
Who pays for the repair or replacement?
copper/raw material: How often do you revise prices?
How do dealers find out about a new price?
dealers: How many active dealers do you have?
How is each one’s discount recorded?
orders: How do reps send orders to the factory?
Have any orders gone missing recently?
fakes: How do you tell them apart?
online: Which marketplaces do you sell on?
What’s the most common complaint there?
production: What stops the line most — parts, power or people?

seasons: PK fan season builds from February/March and peaks April–July; cable and wiring demand follows construction (post-monsoon to spring) and budget/price changes; lighting and decorative lights spike before Eid, weddings and Independence Day (14 August); load-shedding drives demand for DC/inverter fans and rechargeable lights. UAE: AC and cooling-related peaks in summer, project lighting through the construction season, Ramadan and Diwali decoration lighting. Canada: holiday lighting (November– December), spring–summer renovation and construction for wiring.
care: No electrical safety, wiring or rating advice; note only operational issues like “claims of overheating” as quality complaints.
Shocks, electrical fires or burns — pi stops and points to emergency services.
Never help put false certification marks, fake ratings or another brand’s name on products — decline.
Copper scrap or copper theft discussed: note as loss; do not help dispose of stolen copper.
Customer and electrician details in warranty registers: roles only; no names or numbers stored.
Under-invoicing imports or misdeclaring components: decline plainly.
build_ideas: Serial-number registration: each unit’s serial, model, batch and dispatch dealer, with warranty start on sale.
Warranty claim app: dealer scans the serial, uploads photos, and the claim is checked against records.
Genuine-product check by QR or code on the box that customers or dealers can verify on WhatsApp.
Seasonal build plan: target stock by model by week, with progress against plan.
Dealer price list publisher: one live price list per dealer tier, updated when copper changes.
Dealer credit and scheme ledger with eligibility and claims checked against invoices.
Sales rep order app feeding a single order book with status back to the rep.
Service-centre ticket tracker with turnaround time and repeat-fault reporting by model.
Marketplace order bridge for Daraz/Amazon/Noon to see online and dealer allocations together.
Copper and component consumption log by production batch.
Electrician loyalty program with unique coupon codes and single redemption.
Owner dashboard: sales by region and model, stock cover, warranty rate per model, receivables.
